body: Chief: CONFIRMED as proposed — PseudonymizedText retains the source detection receipt and the destination receipt (empty spans), and its keyed canonical payload rendering binds policy, key, text, offset map and both receipt identities, so the capability proves which detector/config certified the payload and receipts cannot be swapped or dropped. Versioning exactly as you say: pseudo/v2 is a new rendering; pseudo/v1 (P0-2) is left intact and the ADR D6 records both with the rule that a rendering change is always a new version. One law to add: a payload with a swapped or absent detection receipt yields a different digest AND fails evaluate (not merely differs). Sequence: after P0-2 lands.
